research_question: Hurricanes with more feminine names are perceived as less threatening and hence lead to fewer precautionary measures by the general public.

ivs.description: Continuous masculinity–femininity index for hurricane names (higher = more feminine), rated by independent coders; the main continuous predictor of interest.
Binary gender indicator of the hurricane name (0 = male, 1 = female); an alternative main predictor representing female-coded names.

dv.description: Total number of deaths caused by the hurricane (used as a proxy for the public's precautionary response); the analysis modeled log(1 + alldeaths).

controls.description: Maximum wind speed of the hurricane at the time of landfall (hurricane intensity control).
Minimum central pressure of the hurricane at landfall (hurricane intensity control).
Saffir–Simpson scale category of the hurricane (1–5), included as an intensity/control variable.
Estimated property damage normalized to 2015 dollars (control for storm impact/severity).
Year the hurricane occurred (included in some specifications to account for time trends).

extracted_analysis.analysis_code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Load data
_df = pd.read_csv("hurricane.csv")

# Keep relevant columns and drop rows with missing values
cols = [
    "alldeaths",
    "masfem",
    "gender_mf",
    "wind",
    "min",
    "category",
    "ndam15",
    "year",
    "elapsedyrs",
]

df = _df[cols].copy()

df = df.dropna()

# Outcome: log(1+deaths) to reduce skew
# Add small constant to avoid log(0)
df["log_deaths"] = np.log1p(df["alldeaths"])

# Standardize continuous predictors for interpretability
for c in ["masfem", "wind", "min", "ndam15", "year", "elapsedyrs"]:
    df[c + "_z"] = (df[c] - df[c].mean()) / df[c].std(ddof=0)

# Model 1: masfem + hurricane intensity controls
X1 = df[["masfem_z", "wind_z", "min_z", "category", "ndam15_z"]]
X1 = sm.add_constant(X1)
model1 = sm.OLS(df["log_deaths"], X1).fit(cov_type="HC3")

# Model 2: binary gender + same controls
X2 = df[["gender_mf", "wind_z", "min_z", "category", "ndam15_z"]]
X2 = sm.add_constant(X2)
model2 = sm.OLS(df["log_deaths"], X2).fit(cov_type="HC3")

# Model 3: add year to account for time trends
X3 = df[["masfem_z", "wind_z", "min_z", "category", "ndam15_z", "year_z"]]
X3 = sm.add_constant(X3)
model3 = sm.OLS(df["log_deaths"], X3).fit(cov_type="HC3")

# Print concise results
print("N:", len(df))

def summarize(model, key):
    coef = model.params[key]
    se = model.bse[key]
    p = model.pvalues[key]
    return coef, se, p

print("Model1 (masfem):", summarize(model1, "masfem_z"))
print("Model2 (gender_mf):", summarize(model2, "gender_mf"))
print("Model3 (masfem + year):", summarize(model3, "masfem_z"))
